prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `heading_offset` option. It is checked in `Markdown.__init__`: any value other than a whole number from 0 to 5 raises `ValueError`, including `True`, `1.0` and `'1'`. A new tree processor called `heading_offset` (priority 25) then shifts every h1–h6 element, never past h6. It runs before `toc`, so `toc_tokens` and `toc_depth` see the shifted levels. It shifts hash, underline and `md_in_html` headings, including `<h1 markdown="1">`. Raw HTML headings that Markdown passes through unchanged are not shifted. On the command line, `--heading-offset N` exits with a usage error if N is outside 0–5. Tests, docs (library, cli, toc) and a changelog entry are added, and the full suite passes (`python3 -m unittest discover tests`: OK, 112 skipped). I did not run flake8 because it isn't installed.
